topics.suggested_exercise: Friction log: next time an agent (Claude Code, Copilot, whichever) does something unexpected - refuses, loops, silently expands scope - stop and write one sentence: what you asked, what it did, and which category it falls into (technical constraint / effort-vs-value / scope creep). Do this 5 times across a week, then read them together. Look for a pattern tied to a specific tool (e.g. 'I keep hitting scope creep with Copilot specifically on multi-file changes') - that pattern is the lesson, not generic advice.

topics.title: Capstone: reframe an existing project through a performance-computing lens
topics.suggested_exercise: Take one piece of facebots or the learning platform's curation logic and ask: if this had to serve 1,000x the load, what would break first - latency, cost, rate limits, ordering guarantees? Sketch (on paper, 10 minutes, no code) how you'd introduce batching, caching, or a queue to fix it. No build required - the point is to see your own hobby project through a perf-computing lens.
